clue.text: Some food said to be lacking taste

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so the spoken word stands in for a different spelling

blocks.note: a course is one part of a meal, such as the soup or the pudding

explanation.surface: A diner complains that one dish, it is reported, is bland.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse manners or jokes are vulgar, showing a want of refinement or good judgement.

clue.text: Stylish clothing one female's to organise

indicators.note: clothing something means wrapping it, so one word dresses the other

blocks.note: classy means stylish
the Roman numeral one
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A fashionable outfit that a woman has to put together.
explanation.definitionFit: To classify is to sort into categories, a way of organising.

clue.text: Matilda oddly ignored assistant

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are disregarded, leaving only the even-placed ones

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A girl called Matilda was strangely overlooked by a helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An aid can be a person who helps, an assistant or aide.

clue.text: Small hole by the foreign river for a duck

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a hole can be a squalid little dwelling
le is French for the
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A modest hovel near a river abroad suits a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places one piece next to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoveller is a dabbling duck named for its broad, shovel-shaped bill.

clue.text: Station providing drink before the office

indicators.note: before tells us the drink's word comes first, with the next word following it

blocks.note: the plainest drink of all
'the office' is old slang for the toilet; loo is the British everyday word for it

explanation.surface: A commuter's account of a station with a café near the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The office' reads as a workplace, but it is a jokey euphemism for the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo is a major London railway terminus, so it is an example of a station.

clue.text: A black sole circles a shellfish

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: taken as written
BL is an abbreviation for black
taken as written
sole means single, only one

explanation.surface: A dark-coloured flatfish swims round some shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like the fish but means single, and 'circles' acts only on the abbreviation for black, which wraps the second 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail with an ear-shaped shell, so a shellfish.

clue.text: Mourn headless heron

indicators.note: without a head means the opening letter is chopped off

blocks.note: to regret a loss is to mourn it

explanation.surface: Grieving for a heron that has lost its head.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white wading bird belonging to the heron family.

clue.text: Swimming Liffey and Loire for a carefree existence

indicators.note: swimming letters are moving about, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dip in the rivers of Dublin and France makes for an easy life.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liffey runs through Dublin and the Loire through France; 'and' simply joins the two names.
explanation.definitionFit: The life of Riley is an idiom for a comfortable, worry-free way of living.

clue.text: Cook's key?

blocks.note: surface reading: a gadget in the kitchen, such as a tin key
setter's reading: Alastair Cook, England cricket captain, whose key role was starting the innings

explanation.walkthrough: A key opens a lock and a can-opener is kitchen kit; Alastair Cook batted first for England.
explanation.definitionFit: A key or tin-opener is something that opens, and the cricketer Cook was England's leading opening batsman.

clue.text: Act stupidly and get lost

blocks.note: first meaning, split differently
second meaning: go away, clear off

explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words it is 'be a tit', to behave like an idiot; read as two it means scram.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is an idiom ordering someone to leave, and be a tit means act the fool.

clue.text: Stars with European city lawyer

blocks.note: with and and both mean together with
the Italian capital
a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A list of celebrities, a city in Europe and a legal adviser, like a gossip column.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, a named group of stars, also home to a famous galaxy.

clue.text: Anger about loud gun

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word wraps itself round the other

blocks.note: to rile someone is to anger them
f is forte, the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a noisy firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, one kind of gun.

clue.text: Important member of the great and good welcoming a foreigner

indicators.note: welcoming a guest means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.clueFragment: member of the great and good
blocks.note: a saint is one of the truly good, abbreviated St
an alien is a foreign national

explanation.surface: A prominent establishment figure plays host to someone from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The great and good' suggests the establishment, but only a saint, abbreviated St, is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient points are the most noticeable or significant ones, hence important.

clue.text: Doctor haggling about gold and sulphur — chemical inducing euphoria

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the metal

blocks.note: taken as written
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A physician bargaining over precious and other elements, about a drug that makes one euphoric.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughing gas is nitrous oxide, an anaesthetic that causes giddy elation.

clue.text: Centre of learning's large book about Celtic's result

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the book wraps round the club's letter

blocks.note: the Open University, a British distance-learning institution
a tome is a big heavy volume
C is a standard abbreviation for Celtic

explanation.surface: A university's hefty volume on Celtic football club and how things turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: OU, the Open University, goes in front; the tome then contains C.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end result of something.

clue.text: This could be rude

blocks.note: surface reading: describing a vulgar expression
setter's reading: the word rude itself has four letters, so it fits the description literally

explanation.walkthrough: Swear words are traditionally called by this name; the joke is that the harmless word 'rude' also qualifies by its length.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-letter word is a swear word, and 'rude' is literally a word of four letters.

clue.text: Vessel that may dispatch a pod

definitions.text: Vessel that may dispatch a pod

blocks.clueFragment: Vessel that may dispatch a pod
blocks.note: surface reading: a spacecraft launching an escape pod
setter's reading: a pod is a group of whales, which this boat was built to hunt and kill

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pod' suggests a capsule launched from a spaceship; 'dispatch' means kill, and the pod is a school of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaleboat is a long narrow rowing boat used in whaling to chase and kill whales.

clue.text: Bile about fashionable journalist initially hard to take in

indicators.note: about here means round and about, so the letters are scattered and rearranged
initially says those words come at the start, ahead of the rearranged letters

blocks.note: in means fashionable
an ed, or editor, is a journalist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trendy writer's spiteful ranting is hard to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like it takes a first letter, but it puts IN and ED at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Inedible food cannot be eaten, so it is hard to swallow and digest.

clue.text: Comic's cleaner story when with vicar on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear a word, so a soundalike spelling is wanted

blocks.note: a char or charwoman is a British cleaning lady
a story can be a fib
a chaplain is a clergyman, like a vicar

explanation.surface: A comedian's tale about a cleaning lady and a vicar heard in a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was the great silent-film comedian, so a famous comic.

clue.text: At home drink I had is flavourless

blocks.note: being in means being at home
a small drink
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A drink I had at home tasted of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food lacks taste, so it is bland and without flavour.

clue.text: Guard's request to turn in vehicle

indicators.note: in places one item within another

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
PTO, please turn over, is printed at the foot of a page

explanation.surface: A security guard asks for a car to make a U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A captor holds a prisoner, so keeps guard over them as a jailer would.

clue.text: Provide refreshment? It's right to fill this hole!

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it, so one letter is placed within

blocks.note: to cater is to supply food and drink
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A caterer is told that the proper thing is to fill this pit with food.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a large hollow in the ground, a kind of hole.

clue.text: Grates start to rust on joints

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of rust
the ankles are joints of the leg

explanation.surface: A mechanic describes grates corroding at their hinges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grates' looks like a noun for fireplace bars; here it is a verb, as in 'it grates on me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles irritates persistently, just as something that grates jars on the nerves.

clue.text: Mostly big, old and slow

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: large means big
O is an abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Something largely big, aged and sluggish, perhaps an elderly animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction meaning a slow, broad tempo.

clue.text: Tart sometimes looked stewed

blocks.note: a tart is sometimes a kind of pie
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A tart that seemed to have been cooked slowly, as in a bakery review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stewed' fits the cooking picture, but here it is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie-eyed and stewed are both informal words for drunk.

clue.text: Row about good golfer

indicators.note: about means around, so the row encircles the other letter

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: An argument concerning a fine player of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger Woods is one of the most famous golfers of all time.

clue.text: Will one snap when gatecrashers do this?

definitions.text: Will one snap when gatecrashers do this?

blocks.clueFragment: Will one snap when gatecrashers do this?
blocks.note: surface reading: will a host lose their temper when uninvited guests turn up?
setter's reading: snap is a photograph, and gatecrashers here jump uninvited into someone else's picture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap' looks like losing one's temper, but it means taking a photo; the gatecrashers are people intruding into a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To photobomb is to appear unexpectedly in the background of someone else's photograph, gatecrashing the picture.

clue.text: Put gold round a blade

indicators.note: Put round tells us to set one piece around the other

blocks.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to gild the edge of a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' merely opens the instruction, which reads as a command to set gold around the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is a rowing blade, and blade is also used for the oar as a whole.

clue.text: Stupid person starts to deliver smart answers

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled and senseless, so these letters are jumbled
starts are opening letters, so only the first of each following word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
opening letters of deliver and smart

explanation.surface: A foolish individual begins giving clever replies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid person' reads as one insult, but the first word is the anagram signal acting on the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Responds is the verb meaning replies, as is answers in its verb sense.

clue.text: Something rude to do is eating very fast

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: staring at people is considered rude
V is the usual abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A dinner-table complaint that it is impolite to eat too quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' suggests speed, but it is the verb meaning go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve, like to fast, is to go without food.
